_doc: Kho điểm ngữ pháp tiếng Nhật (JLPT N5→N1 ↔ A1→C1) của LexKite. 100% tự soạn: tên điểm, câu "Can …" và ví dụ là của LexKite, không chép danh mục điểm của Japan Foundation/JEES hay sách giáo trình (CONTENT-RULES §1). level = bậc CEFR tương ứng (N5=A1, N4=A2, N3=B1, N2=B2, N1=C1), jlpt = cấp JLPT; lessons = id bài ja (chưa có → []); tenses = khóa của scripts/target/conj-ja.mjs (FORMS); kiểm: node scripts/content-qa/grammar-map-check.mjs --tl ja; id điểm KHÔNG đổi/tái dùng.

points.name: X wa Y desu: identity and profession
points.can_do_en: Can say who someone is and what they do with は and です.
points.example: わたしは田中です。学生です。
points.example_en: I am Tanaka. I am a student.

points.name: ではありません / じゃないです
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is not so, in polite style.
points.example: これはペンではありません。
points.example_en: This is not a pen.

points.name: でした / ではありませんでした
points.can_do_en: Can say what something was or was not in the past.
points.example: 昨日は休みでした。
points.example_en: Yesterday was a day off.

points.name: か: yes/no questions
points.can_do_en: Can turn a statement into a question by adding か.
points.example: あなたは先生ですか。
points.example_en: Are you a teacher?

points.name: は: topic marker
points.can_do_en: Can mark the topic of a sentence with は.
points.example: 私は犬が好きです。
points.example_en: As for me, I like dogs.

points.name: も: also, too
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is also true with も.
points.example: 田中さんも学生です。
points.example_en: Mr. Tanaka is also a student.

points.name: の: possession and attribution
points.can_do_en: Can link two nouns with の to show who owns something or what kind it is.
points.example: これは私の本です。
points.example_en: This is my book.

points.name: が: subject and likes/abilities
points.can_do_en: Can use が with 好き, 上手 and similar words to name what is liked or known.
points.example: 兄は料理が上手です。
points.example_en: My older brother is good at cooking.

points.name: を: direct object
points.can_do_en: Can mark the thing that an action is done to with を.
points.example: 毎朝パンを食べます。
points.example_en: I eat bread every morning.

points.name: に: point in time
points.can_do_en: Can say when something happens with に and a time word.
points.example: 七時に起きます。
points.example_en: I get up at seven.

points.name: に / へ: destination
points.can_do_en: Can say where someone goes with に or へ.
points.example: 明日、学校へ行きます。
points.example_en: Tomorrow I will go to school.

points.name: で: place of action
points.can_do_en: Can say where an action takes place with で.
points.example: 図書館で勉強します。
points.example_en: I study at the library.

points.name: で: means and tool
points.can_do_en: Can say how or with what something is done with で.
points.example: バスで会社へ行きます。
points.example_en: I go to the office by bus.

points.name: と: with, and
points.can_do_en: Can say who you do something with, and list nouns, with と.
points.example: 友達と映画を見ます。
points.example_en: I watch a movie with a friend.

points.name: から / まで: from and until
points.can_do_en: Can say a starting and an ending point in time or place.
points.example: 九時から五時まで働きます。
points.example_en: I work from nine to five.

points.name: や: listing examples
points.can_do_en: Can list a few examples of many with や.
points.example: 机の上に本やノートがあります。
points.example_en: There are books and notebooks on the desk.

points.name: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
points.can_do_en: Can point to things near, far and unknown with これ, それ, あれ and どれ.
points.example: それは何ですか。
points.example_en: What is that?

points.name: この・その・あの + noun
points.can_do_en: Can point to a noun with この, その and あの.
points.example: あの人は先生です。
points.example_en: That person is a teacher.

points.name: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ
points.can_do_en: Can ask and tell where something is with place words.
points.example: トイレはあそこです。
points.example_en: The restroom is over there.

points.name: ある and いる: existence
points.can_do_en: Can say that things exist with ある and that people or animals exist with いる.
points.example: 庭に猫がいます。
points.example_en: There is a cat in the garden.

points.name: place に noun が あります
points.can_do_en: Can say what is in a place using に and が.
points.example: 部屋にテレビがあります。
points.example_en: There is a TV in the room.

points.name: 上・下・中・前・後ろ・隣
points.can_do_en: Can say where something is with position words such as 上, 下 and 隣.
points.example: 机の下に鞄があります。
points.example_en: There is a bag under the desk.

points.name: ます form: polite present and future
points.can_do_en: Can use the ます form for habits and future plans.
points.example: 毎日、水を飲みます。
points.example_en: I drink water every day.

points.name: ません: polite negative
points.can_do_en: Can say you do not do something with ません.
points.example: 私は肉を食べません。
points.example_en: I do not eat meat.

points.name: ました: polite past
points.can_do_en: Can say what you did with ました.
points.example: 昨日、友達に会いました。
points.example_en: Yesterday I met a friend.

points.name: ませんでした: polite past negative
points.can_do_en: Can say you did not do something with ませんでした.
points.example: 今朝は何も食べませんでした。
points.example_en: I did not eat anything this morning.

points.name: ましょう: let's
points.can_do_en: Can suggest doing something together with ましょう.
points.example: 一緒に昼ご飯を食べましょう。
points.example_en: Let's eat lunch together.

points.name: ませんか: would you like to
points.can_do_en: Can invite someone politely with ませんか.
points.example: コーヒーを飲みませんか。
points.example_en: Would you like to have coffee?

points.name: たい: want to do
points.can_do_en: Can say what you want to do with the stem and たい.
points.example: 日本へ行きたいです。
points.example_en: I want to go to Japan.

points.name: てください: please do
points.can_do_en: Can ask someone to do something with てください.
points.example: ここに名前を書いてください。
points.example_en: Please write your name here.

points.name: い-adjectives: present
points.can_do_en: Can describe things with い-adjectives before です or a noun.
points.example: この部屋は広いです。
points.example_en: This room is spacious.

points.name: い-adjectives: くないです
points.can_do_en: Can negate an い-adjective with くない.
points.example: この本は高くないです。
points.example_en: This book is not expensive.

points.name: い-adjectives: かったです
points.can_do_en: Can put an い-adjective in the past with かった.
points.example: 昨日は暑かったです。
points.example_en: It was hot yesterday.

points.name: な-adjectives
points.can_do_en: Can use な-adjectives with です and with な before a noun.
points.example: 静かな町が好きです。
points.example_en: I like quiet towns.

points.name: な-adjectives: negative and past
points.can_do_en: Can negate and past-mark a な-adjective with ではありません and でした.
points.example: あの店は便利ではありません。
points.example_en: That shop is not convenient.

points.name: adjective + noun
points.can_do_en: Can put an adjective before a noun to describe it.
points.example: 大きい犬を見ました。
points.example_en: I saw a big dog.

points.name: adjective て-form: and
points.can_do_en: Can join two descriptions with the て-form of an adjective.
points.example: この町は小さくて静かです。
points.example_en: This town is small and quiet.

points.name: 何・誰・いつ・どこ・どう
points.can_do_en: Can ask basic questions with 何, 誰, いつ, どこ and どう.
points.example: 誕生日はいつですか。
points.example_en: When is your birthday?

points.name: いくら: how much
points.can_do_en: Can ask the price of something with いくら.
points.example: このりんごはいくらですか。
points.example_en: How much is this apple?

points.name: numbers 1–10,000
points.can_do_en: Can say and read numbers up to ten thousand.
points.example: この本は千五百円です。
points.example_en: This book costs fifteen hundred yen.

points.name: clock time: 時・分
points.can_do_en: Can tell the time with 時 and 分.
points.example: 今、三時十五分です。
points.example_en: It is now a quarter past three.

points.name: dates and days of the week
points.can_do_en: Can say the date and the day of the week.
points.example: 今日は五月三日、月曜日です。
points.example_en: Today is Monday, May third.

points.name: ひとつ・ふたつ: native counting
points.can_do_en: Can count things up to ten with the native counting words.
points.example: りんごを三つください。
points.example_en: Please give me three apples.

points.name: 〜人: counting people
points.can_do_en: Can count people with 人, including ひとり and ふたり.
points.example: 家族は四人です。
points.example_en: There are four people in my family.

points.name: 〜枚・〜本・〜個
points.can_do_en: Can count flat things, long things and small things.
points.example: ペンを二本買いました。
points.example_en: I bought two pens.

points.name: 好き・嫌い・上手・下手
points.can_do_en: Can say what you like, dislike or do well with が.
points.example: 私は音楽が好きです。
points.example_en: I like music.

points.name: set expressions and greetings
points.can_do_en: Can use basic greetings and polite set phrases.
points.example: ありがとうございます。どういたしまして。
points.example_en: Thank you. You're welcome.

points.name: word order: verb last
points.can_do_en: Can build a sentence with the verb at the end.
points.example: 私は毎日学校で日本語を勉強します。
points.example_en: I study Japanese at school every day.

points.name: よく・ときどき・あまり・ぜんぜん
points.can_do_en: Can say how often you do something with frequency words.
points.example: 私はあまりテレビを見ません。
points.example_en: I do not watch TV very often.

points.name: とても・すこし・たくさん
points.can_do_en: Can say how much or how many with とても, すこし and たくさん.
points.example: 京都にはお寺がたくさんあります。
points.example_en: There are many temples in Kyoto.

points.name: 行く・来る・帰る
points.can_do_en: Can talk about going, coming and returning home.
points.example: 毎晩、八時に家へ帰ります。
points.example_en: I return home at eight every night.

points.name: polite style です・ます
points.can_do_en: Can speak in the polite style that is safe with everyone.
points.example: はじめまして。どうぞよろしくお願いします。
points.example_en: Nice to meet you. Please treat me well.

points.name: て-form formation
points.can_do_en: Can build the て-form of verbs from all three verb groups.
points.example: 飲んでください。
points.example_en: Please drink.

points.name: ている: ongoing action
points.can_do_en: Can say that an action is in progress with ている.
points.example: 今、本を読んでいます。
points.example_en: I am reading a book now.

points.name: ている: resulting state and habit
points.can_do_en: Can describe a state that resulted from an action with ている.
points.example: 私は東京に住んでいます。
points.example_en: I live in Tokyo.

points.name: てもいい: permission
points.can_do_en: Can ask for and give permission with てもいいです.
points.example: 写真を撮ってもいいですか。
points.example_en: May I take a photo?

points.name: てはいけない: prohibition
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is not allowed with てはいけません.
points.example: ここで食べてはいけません。
points.example_en: You must not eat here.

points.name: ない form
points.can_do_en: Can build the plain negative with ない.
points.example: 私は朝ご飯を食べない。
points.example_en: I do not eat breakfast.

points.name: ないでください: please do not
points.can_do_en: Can ask someone not to do something with ないでください.
points.example: ここで写真を撮らないでください。
points.example_en: Please do not take photos here.

points.name: なければならない: must
points.can_do_en: Can say what you have to do with なければならない.
points.example: 明日までに宿題を出さなければなりません。
points.example_en: I have to hand in my homework by tomorrow.

points.name: なくてもいい: need not
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is not necessary with なくてもいい.
points.example: 明日は来なくてもいいです。
points.example_en: You do not have to come tomorrow.

points.name: た form: plain past
points.can_do_en: Can build the plain past with た.
points.example: 昨日は映画を見た。
points.example_en: I watched a movie yesterday.

points.name: dictionary form (plain present)
points.can_do_en: Can use the dictionary form as the plain present and future.
points.example: 私は毎朝コーヒーを飲む。
points.example_en: I drink coffee every morning.

points.name: ことができる: can do
points.can_do_en: Can say what you are able to do with ことができる.
points.example: 私は泳ぐことができます。
points.example_en: I can swim.

points.name: たことがある: have done before
points.can_do_en: Can say that you have had an experience with たことがあります.
points.example: 富士山に登ったことがあります。
points.example_en: I have climbed Mount Fuji.

points.name: つもり: intend to
points.can_do_en: Can state an intention with つもりです.
points.example: 来年、日本へ行くつもりです。
points.example_en: I intend to go to Japan next year.

points.name: 前に: before doing
points.can_do_en: Can say that one thing happens before another with 前に.
points.example: 寝る前に歯をみがきます。
points.example_en: I brush my teeth before I go to bed.

points.name: てから・あとで: after doing
points.can_do_en: Can say that one thing happens after another with てから or あとで.
points.example: ご飯を食べてから、出かけます。
points.example_en: After I eat, I will go out.

points.name: ながら: while doing
points.can_do_en: Can say that two actions happen at the same time with ながら.
points.example: 音楽を聞きながら勉強します。
points.example_en: I study while listening to music.

points.name: て-form: sequence of actions
points.can_do_en: Can list actions in order with the て-form.
points.example: 朝起きて、顔を洗って、朝ご飯を食べます。
points.example_en: I get up, wash my face and eat breakfast.

points.name: から: because
points.can_do_en: Can give a reason with から.
points.example: 雨ですから、家にいます。
points.example_en: Because it is raining, I will stay home.

points.name: が・けど: but
points.can_do_en: Can contrast two ideas with が or けど.
points.example: 高いですが、おいしいです。
points.example_en: It is expensive, but it is delicious.

points.name: ので: because (softer)
points.can_do_en: Can give a polite reason with ので.
points.example: 熱があるので、休みます。
points.example_en: Because I have a fever, I will rest.

points.name: でしょう: probably
points.can_do_en: Can make a guess with でしょう.
points.example: 明日は雨でしょう。
points.example_en: It will probably rain tomorrow.

points.name: かもしれない: might
points.can_do_en: Can say something is possible with かもしれません.
points.example: 彼は来ないかもしれません。
points.example_en: He might not come.

points.name: ほうがいい: had better
points.can_do_en: Can give advice with たほうがいい and ないほうがいい.
points.example: 早く寝たほうがいいですよ。
points.example_en: You should go to bed early.

points.name: plain style in casual speech
points.can_do_en: Can speak casually with friends in the plain form.
points.example: 明日、一緒に行く？
points.example_en: Shall we go together tomorrow?

points.name: と思う: I think that
points.can_do_en: Can give an opinion with と思います.
points.example: 明日は雨が降ると思います。
points.example_en: I think it will rain tomorrow.

points.name: と言う: quote what was said
points.can_do_en: Can report what someone said with と言いました.
points.example: 先生は明日休みだと言いました。
points.example_en: The teacher said tomorrow is a day off.

points.name: こと: turning a verb into a noun
points.can_do_en: Can turn a verb into a noun with こと.
points.example: 私の趣味は本を読むことです。
points.example_en: My hobby is reading books.

points.name: の: turning a verb into a noun
points.can_do_en: Can use の to treat an action as a thing.
points.example: 歌うのが好きです。
points.example_en: I like singing.

points.name: noun-modifying clause
points.can_do_en: Can put a plain-form clause before a noun to describe it.
points.example: 昨日買った本は面白いです。
points.example_en: The book I bought yesterday is interesting.

points.name: くなる・になる: become
points.can_do_en: Can say that something becomes a state with くなる and になる.
points.example: だんだん寒くなります。
points.example_en: It gets colder little by little.

points.name: くする・にする: make
points.can_do_en: Can say that you make something a state with くする and にする.
points.example: 音を小さくしてください。
points.example_en: Please turn the sound down.

points.name: より・のほうが: comparing two
points.can_do_en: Can compare two things with より and のほうが.
points.example: 電車のほうがバスより速いです。
points.example_en: The train is faster than the bus.

points.name: 一番: the most
points.can_do_en: Can say which is the most with 一番.
points.example: 果物の中でりんごが一番好きです。
points.example_en: Among fruits I like apples best.

points.name: そうです: looks like
points.can_do_en: Can say how something looks with the stem and そうです.
points.example: このケーキはおいしそうです。
points.example_en: This cake looks delicious.

points.name: すぎる: too much
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is too much with すぎる.
points.example: 昨日はお酒を飲みすぎました。
points.example_en: I drank too much yesterday.

points.name: あげる・くれる・もらう
points.can_do_en: Can say who gives to whom with あげる, くれる and もらう.
points.example: 友達が私に本をくれました。
points.example_en: A friend gave me a book.

points.name: てあげる・てくれる・てもらう
points.can_do_en: Can say that someone does a favor with てあげる, てくれる and てもらう.
points.example: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
points.example_en: My mother cooked for me.

points.name: てみる: try doing
points.can_do_en: Can say that you try doing something with てみる.
points.example: この服を着てみてもいいですか。
points.example_en: May I try on these clothes?

points.name: てしまう: finish, regret
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is finished or regretted with てしまう.
points.example: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
points.example_en: I forgot my homework, unfortunately.

points.name: ておく: do in advance
points.can_do_en: Can say that you prepare something in advance with ておく.
points.example: 旅行の前にホテルを予約しておきます。
points.example_en: I book the hotel before the trip.

points.name: たら: if / when
points.can_do_en: Can say what happens if or when something is done with たら.
points.example: 雨が降ったら、行きません。
points.example_en: If it rains, I will not go.

points.name: と: if (natural result)
points.can_do_en: Can say that something always follows with と.
points.example: 春になると、桜が咲きます。
points.example_en: When spring comes, cherry trees bloom.

points.name: ば: if (condition)
points.can_do_en: Can state a condition with the ば form.
points.example: 安ければ、買います。
points.example_en: If it is cheap, I will buy it.

points.name: potential form: can do
points.can_do_en: Can say you can do something with the potential form.
points.example: 私は漢字が読めます。
points.example_en: I can read kanji.

points.name: volitional form: let's, I will
points.can_do_en: Can make a casual suggestion or resolve with the volitional form.
points.example: 一緒に帰ろう。
points.example_en: Let's go home together.

points.name: ようになる: come to be able
points.can_do_en: Can say that a change has taken place with ようになる.
points.example: 日本語が話せるようになりました。
points.example_en: I have come to be able to speak Japanese.

points.name: 〜回・〜冊・〜台・〜杯
points.can_do_en: Can count occasions, books, machines and cups.
points.example: 一日に三回薬を飲みます。
points.example_en: I take medicine three times a day.

points.name: 〜時間・〜日・〜週間
points.can_do_en: Can say how long something takes with duration words.
points.example: 毎日二時間勉強します。
points.example_en: I study for two hours every day.

points.name: だけ・しか〜ない
points.can_do_en: Can say only with だけ and しか〜ない.
points.example: 百円しかありません。
points.example_en: I have only one hundred yen.

points.name: でも: even, or something
points.can_do_en: Can suggest an example with でも.
points.example: お茶でも飲みませんか。
points.example_en: Would you like some tea or something?

points.name: ね・よ: sentence-final particles
points.can_do_en: Can seek agreement with ね and give new information with よ.
points.example: 今日はいい天気ですね。
points.example_en: Nice weather today, isn't it?

points.name: けど・が: softening a request
points.can_do_en: Can open or soften a request with けど or が.
points.example: すみませんが、駅はどこですか。
points.example_en: Excuse me, where is the station?

points.name: どんな・どう・どうして
points.can_do_en: Can ask what kind, how and why.
points.example: どうして日本語を勉強しますか。
points.example_en: Why do you study Japanese?

points.name: 何か・誰か・どこか
points.can_do_en: Can say something, someone or somewhere with か.
points.example: 何か飲みますか。
points.example_en: Will you drink something?

points.name: 何も・誰も・どこにも
points.can_do_en: Can say nothing, nobody or nowhere with も and a negative.
points.example: 今日は誰も来ませんでした。
points.example_en: Nobody came today.

points.name: はず: should be
points.can_do_en: Can say what you expect to be true with はず.
points.example: 彼はもう家にいるはずです。
points.example_en: He should already be at home.

points.name: ことになる・ことにする
points.can_do_en: Can say what has been decided with ことになる and ことにする.
points.example: 来月、引っ越すことにしました。
points.example_en: I decided to move next month.

points.name: passive form: られる
points.can_do_en: Can say what happened to someone with the passive form.
points.example: 私は先生にほめられました。
points.example_en: I was praised by my teacher.

points.name: indirect passive: being troubled
points.can_do_en: Can say that something unwelcome happened to you with the passive.
points.example: 雨に降られて、服がぬれました。
points.example_en: I got caught in the rain and my clothes got wet.

points.name: passive without an agent
points.can_do_en: Can state a fact without naming who did it using the passive.
points.example: この橋は百年前に作られました。
points.example_en: This bridge was built a hundred years ago.

points.name: causative form: させる
points.can_do_en: Can say that you make or let someone do something.
points.example: 母は弟に野菜を食べさせました。
points.example_en: My mother made my brother eat vegetables.

points.name: causative: letting someone
points.can_do_en: Can say that you let someone do what they want.
points.example: 先生は学生に自由に意見を言わせました。
points.example_en: The teacher let the students speak their minds.

points.name: causative passive: being made to
points.can_do_en: Can say that you were made to do something.
points.example: 子どものころ、ピーマンを食べさせられました。
points.example_en: As a child I was made to eat green peppers.

points.name: させてください: please let me
points.can_do_en: Can ask permission humbly with させてください.
points.example: 私に説明させてください。
points.example_en: Please let me explain.

points.name: ば-form: all verb groups
points.can_do_en: Can build the ば-form of verbs and adjectives.
points.example: 時間があれば、手伝います。
points.example_en: If I have time, I will help.

points.name: たら: discovery and past
points.can_do_en: Can describe what you found after doing something with たら.
points.example: 家に帰ったら、手紙が届いていました。
points.example_en: When I got home, a letter had arrived.

points.name: なら: if it is the case
points.can_do_en: Can respond to what someone said with なら.
points.example: 行くなら、早く出たほうがいいです。
points.example_en: If you are going, you should leave early.

points.name: choosing と・ば・たら・なら
points.can_do_en: Can choose between the four conditionals by meaning.
points.example: 安ければ買いますが、高かったら買いません。
points.example_en: If it is cheap I will buy it, but if it is expensive I will not.

points.name: とき: when
points.can_do_en: Can say when something happens with とき.
points.example: 子どものとき、毎日川で遊びました。
points.example_en: When I was a child I played at the river every day.

points.name: あいだ・うちに: while, before it changes
points.can_do_en: Can say during what time or before it changes with あいだ and うちに.
points.example: 若いうちに、いろいろな国へ行きたいです。
points.example_en: While I am young I want to visit many countries.

points.name: とか・など: for example
points.can_do_en: Can give examples with とか and など.
points.example: 休みの日は、映画とか買い物とかをします。
points.example_en: On days off I do things like watching movies and shopping.

points.name: ように: so that
points.can_do_en: Can say a goal or hope with ように.
points.example: 忘れないように、メモをとります。
points.example_en: I take notes so that I will not forget.

points.name: ために: in order to
points.can_do_en: Can say a purpose with ために.
points.example: 日本で働くために、日本語を勉強しています。
points.example_en: I study Japanese in order to work in Japan.

points.name: ため: because of
points.can_do_en: Can give a formal reason with ため.
points.example: 事故のため、電車が遅れています。
points.example_en: The train is late because of an accident.

points.name: ようだ・みたいだ: seems
points.can_do_en: Can say how something seems with ようだ and みたいだ.
points.example: 彼は疲れているようです。
points.example_en: He seems to be tired.

points.name: らしい: apparently
points.can_do_en: Can pass on what you heard with らしい.
points.example: あの店は人気があるらしいです。
points.example_en: Apparently that shop is popular.

points.name: そうだ: I heard that
points.can_do_en: Can report hearsay with plain form and そうだ.
points.example: 天気予報によると、明日は雪だそうです。
points.example_en: According to the forecast, it will snow tomorrow.

points.name: そうだ: looks like (appearance)
points.can_do_en: Can say how something looks about to happen with そうだ.
points.example: 今にも雨が降りそうです。
points.example_en: It looks like it will rain any moment.

points.name: みたい: like, similar to
points.can_do_en: Can compare things casually with みたい.
points.example: 彼女は子どもみたいに笑います。
points.example_en: She laughs like a child.

points.name: はず・わけ: expectation and reason
points.can_do_en: Can express expectation and logical reason with はず and わけ.
points.example: 毎日練習しているから、上手なわけです。
points.example_en: Since you practice every day, it is no wonder you are good.

points.name: のに: even though
points.can_do_en: Can express unexpected contrast with のに.
points.example: 勉強したのに、試験に落ちました。
points.example_en: I studied, yet I failed the exam.

points.name: ので・から・ため: choosing a reason
points.can_do_en: Can choose between ので, から and ため for the right tone.
points.example: 急いでいるので、先に行きます。
points.example_en: Since I'm in a hurry, I'll go ahead.

points.name: て-form as a reason
points.can_do_en: Can give a reason with the て-form.
points.example: ニュースを聞いて、びっくりしました。
points.example_en: I was surprised when I heard the news.

points.name: ながら: although
points.can_do_en: Can show contrast with ながら.
points.example: 知っていながら、教えてくれませんでした。
points.example_en: Although he knew, he did not tell me.

points.name: ていく・てくる: direction of change
points.can_do_en: Can describe change toward or away from now with ていく and てくる.
points.example: 日本語が少しずつ上手になってきました。
points.example_en: My Japanese has gradually become better.

points.name: てある: state left on purpose
points.can_do_en: Can describe a state someone prepared with てある.
points.example: 窓が開けてあります。
points.example_en: The window has been left open.

points.name: ている: already done
points.can_do_en: Can say that an action is already finished with ている.
points.example: もう宿題は終わっています。
points.example_en: The homework is already finished.

points.name: たばかり: just did
points.can_do_en: Can say that something just happened with たばかり.
points.example: さっき起きたばかりです。
points.example_en: I just got up a moment ago.

points.name: ところ: about to, in the middle of
points.can_do_en: Can say what stage an action is at with ところ.
points.example: 今、ご飯を食べているところです。
points.example_en: I am in the middle of eating now.

points.name: ばかり: nothing but
points.can_do_en: Can say that only one kind keeps happening with ばかり.
points.example: 弟はゲームばかりしています。
points.example_en: My brother does nothing but play games.

points.name: さえ・まで・すら: even
points.can_do_en: Can stress an extreme case with さえ and まで.
points.example: 子どもさえ知っていることです。
points.example_en: Even a child knows it.

points.name: ほど・くらい: degree
points.can_do_en: Can say about how much with ほど and くらい.
points.example: 昨日は信じられないほど寒かったです。
points.example_en: Yesterday was so cold it was unbelievable.

points.name: くらい・ぐらい: approximately
points.can_do_en: Can give approximate amounts with くらい.
points.example: 駅まで十分ぐらいかかります。
points.example_en: It takes about ten minutes to the station.

points.name: こそ: emphasis
points.can_do_en: Can stress a point with こそ.
points.example: 今年こそ合格したいです。
points.example_en: This year, of all years, I want to pass.

points.name: として: as
points.can_do_en: Can say in what role something is done with として.
points.example: 留学生として日本に来ました。
points.example_en: I came to Japan as an exchange student.

points.name: について: about
points.can_do_en: Can say the topic of speaking or thinking with について.
points.example: 日本の歴史について調べています。
points.example_en: I am researching Japanese history.

points.name: によって・によると: by, depending on
points.can_do_en: Can say that something depends on or comes from a source with によって.
points.example: 国によって、習慣が違います。
points.example_en: Customs differ depending on the country.

points.name: に対して: toward, in contrast
points.can_do_en: Can say toward whom or in contrast with に対して.
points.example: お客様に対して、失礼なことを言ってはいけません。
points.example_en: You must not say rude things to customers.

points.name: のために: for the sake of
points.can_do_en: Can say for whom you act with のために.
points.example: 家族のために働いています。
points.example_en: I work for the sake of my family.

points.name: に関して: concerning
points.can_do_en: Can introduce a topic with に関して.
points.example: この問題に関して、質問があります。
points.example_en: I have a question about this problem.

points.name: のに: for the purpose of
points.can_do_en: Can say what something is used for with のに.
points.example: この道具は、パンを切るのに使います。
points.example_en: This tool is used for cutting bread.

points.name: ことにする・ことになる
points.can_do_en: Can say decisions and arrangements with ことにする and ことになる.
points.example: 毎日、運動することにしました。
points.example_en: I decided to exercise every day.

points.name: ようにする: try to make a habit
points.can_do_en: Can say that you make an effort to do something regularly.
points.example: なるべく野菜を食べるようにしています。
points.example_en: I try to eat vegetables as much as I can.

points.name: べき: should
points.can_do_en: Can state what ought to be done with べき.
points.example: 約束は守るべきです。
points.example_en: One should keep one's promises.

points.name: わけにはいかない: cannot afford to
points.can_do_en: Can say that circumstances do not allow something.
points.example: 明日は大事な日なので、休むわけにはいきません。
points.example_en: Tomorrow is an important day, so I can't take it off.

points.name: つもり・予定: plan and intention
points.can_do_en: Can tell an intention from a schedule with つもり and 予定.
points.example: 来週、出張する予定です。
points.example_en: I am scheduled to go on a business trip next week.

points.name: なくてはいけない・なきゃ
points.can_do_en: Can say what is needed in more ways, including casual なきゃ.
points.example: もう帰らなきゃ。
points.example_en: I've got to go home now.

points.name: ても・でも: even if
points.can_do_en: Can say that something holds even if a condition is met.
points.example: 雨が降っても、行きます。
points.example_en: I will go even if it rains.

points.name: たらどう: how about
points.can_do_en: Can suggest something gently with たらどう.
points.example: 少し休んだらどうですか。
points.example_en: Why don't you take a rest?

points.name: かどうか: whether or not
points.can_do_en: Can embed a yes/no question with かどうか.
points.example: 彼が来るかどうか分かりません。
points.example_en: I don't know whether he will come.

points.name: embedded questions with か
points.can_do_en: Can embed a wh-question with か.
points.example: 何を食べたいか決めましたか。
points.example_en: Have you decided what you want to eat?

points.name: という: called, named
points.can_do_en: Can name something with という.
points.example: 田中という人から電話がありました。
points.example_en: There was a call from a person named Tanaka.

points.name: ことだ: advice
points.can_do_en: Can give strong advice with ことだ.
points.example: 試験に合格したければ、毎日勉強することだ。
points.example_en: If you want to pass, study every day.

points.name: んです: explaining
points.can_do_en: Can give an explanation or ask for one with んです.
points.example: 頭が痛いんです。
points.example_en: It's that my head hurts.

points.name: ちゃう・ている→てる: casual contractions
points.can_do_en: Can understand casual contractions such as ちゃう and てる.
points.example: 財布を忘れちゃった。
points.example_en: Oops, I forgot my wallet.

points.name: keigo basics: です・ます vs honorific
points.can_do_en: Can tell polite style from honorific and humble speech.
points.example: 先生は、もうお帰りになりました。
points.example_en: The teacher has already gone home.

points.name: お〜になる: honorific
points.can_do_en: Can make an honorific with お〜になる.
points.example: 社長はもうお出かけになりました。
points.example_en: The president has already gone out.

points.name: お〜する: humble
points.can_do_en: Can make a humble expression with お〜する.
points.example: お荷物をお持ちします。
points.example_en: Let me carry your luggage.

points.name: いらっしゃる・おっしゃる・なさる
points.can_do_en: Can use the honorific verbs for being, saying and doing.
points.example: 先生は何とおっしゃいましたか。
points.example_en: What did the teacher say?

points.name: 参る・申す・いたす
points.can_do_en: Can use the humble verbs for going, saying and doing.
points.example: はじめまして。田中と申します。
points.example_en: Nice to meet you. My name is Tanaka.

points.name: お・ご + noun
points.can_do_en: Can add お and ご to nouns to show respect.
points.example: ご家族はお元気ですか。
points.example_en: Is your family well?

points.name: counters with sound changes
points.can_do_en: Can say ippon, sanbon, roppon and similar counter sounds correctly.
points.example: ビールを三本買いました。
points.example_en: I bought three bottles of beer.

points.name: 〜階・〜足・〜匹・〜頭・〜羽
points.can_do_en: Can count floors, pairs, animals and birds.
points.example: 犬が二匹、鳥が三羽います。
points.example_en: There are two dogs and three birds.

points.name: ages, dates and large numbers
points.can_do_en: Can say ages, exact dates and numbers up to hundreds of millions.
points.example: この町の人口は約五十万人です。
points.example_en: The town has a population of about five hundred thousand.

points.name: fractions, percent and ratios
points.can_do_en: Can say fractions, percent and ratios.
points.example: 生徒の三割が自転車で通っています。
points.example_en: Thirty percent of the students commute by bike.

points.name: loanwords and な-adjectives
points.can_do_en: Can use katakana loanwords as nouns and な-adjectives.
points.example: この店はとてもおしゃれです。
points.example_en: This shop is very stylish.

points.name: compound verbs
points.can_do_en: Can understand common compound verbs such as 食べ始める.
points.example: 三時から勉強し始めました。
points.example_en: I started studying at three o'clock.

points.name: 〜的・〜性・〜化
points.can_do_en: Can read and use the suffixes 的, 性 and 化.
points.example: それは一般的な考え方です。
points.example_en: That is a general way of thinking.

points.name: onomatopoeia
points.can_do_en: Can use common sound and mimetic words.
points.example: 雨がざあざあ降っています。
points.example_en: The rain is pouring down.

points.name: fillers and backchannel
points.can_do_en: Can use fillers and backchannel to keep a conversation going.
points.example: ええと、そうですね、少し考えさせてください。
points.example_en: Well, let me think a little.

points.name: そして・それから・それに
points.can_do_en: Can add information with そして, それから and それに.
points.example: このカフェは安いです。それに、静かです。
points.example_en: This cafe is cheap. Besides, it is quiet.

points.name: だから・それで・ですから
points.can_do_en: Can give results with だから, それで and ですから.
points.example: 雨でした。だから、家にいました。
points.example_en: It rained. So I stayed home.

points.name: しかし・でも・ところが
points.can_do_en: Can contrast with しかし, でも and ところが.
points.example: 頑張りました。しかし、だめでした。
points.example_en: I tried hard. However, it did not work out.

points.name: つまり・たとえば
points.can_do_en: Can restate and exemplify with つまり and たとえば.
points.example: つまり、来ないということですか。
points.example_en: So, you mean you won't come?

points.name: honorific verb forms (れる・られる, special verbs)
points.can_do_en: Can pick the right honorific verb form for a superior.
points.example: 先生が本を読まれました。
points.example_en: The teacher read a book.

points.name: humble verb forms
points.can_do_en: Can describe your own actions humbly toward a superior.
points.example: 資料を拝見しました。
points.example_en: I have looked at the documents.

points.name: ございます・でございます
points.can_do_en: Can use ございます in service and formal speech.
points.example: こちらが受付でございます。
points.example_en: This is the reception desk.

points.name: お〜ください: honorific request
points.can_do_en: Can make a polite request with お〜ください.
points.example: こちらでお待ちください。
points.example_en: Please wait here.

points.name: させていただく: humble permission
points.can_do_en: Can use させていただく without overusing it.
points.example: 本日は私が説明させていただきます。
points.example_en: Today I will do the explaining.

points.name: いただく・くださる
points.can_do_en: Can express receiving and giving with polite verbs.
points.example: 先生が教えてくださいました。
points.example_en: The teacher taught me.

points.name: business set phrases
points.can_do_en: Can use phrases such as お世話になっております.
points.example: いつもお世話になっております。
points.example_en: Thank you always for your support.

points.name: email openings and closings
points.can_do_en: Can open and close a formal email in Japanese.
points.example: ご確認のほど、よろしくお願いいたします。
points.example_en: Thank you in advance for your confirmation.

points.name: において: in, at (formal)
points.can_do_en: Can say where or in what field in formal writing.
points.example: この分野において、彼は第一人者です。
points.example_en: In this field, he is a leading authority.

points.name: に関する・についての
points.can_do_en: Can modify a noun with に関する and についての.
points.example: 環境に関する調査が行われました。
points.example_en: A survey about the environment was carried out.

points.name: によると・によれば
points.can_do_en: Can cite a source with によると.
points.example: 新聞によると、来月値上がりするそうです。
points.example_en: According to the newspaper, prices will rise next month.

points.name: に対する・に対して
points.can_do_en: Can express an attitude toward something with に対する.
points.example: 環境問題に対する関心が高まっています。
points.example_en: Interest in environmental problems is growing.

points.name: にしたがって・につれて
points.can_do_en: Can say that things change together with にしたがって and につれて.
points.example: 年をとるにつれて、体力が落ちます。
points.example_en: As one grows older, one's strength declines.

points.name: にとって: for, from the viewpoint of
points.can_do_en: Can say whose viewpoint with にとって.
points.example: 私にとって、家族は一番大切です。
points.example_en: For me, family is the most important thing.

points.name: としては・にしては
points.can_do_en: Can compare against an expectation with にしては.
points.example: 子どもにしては、よく知っています。
points.example_en: He knows a lot for a child.

points.name: を中心に: centering on
points.can_do_en: Can say the center of something with を中心に.
points.example: 駅を中心に、店が集まっています。
points.example_en: Shops are clustered around the station.

points.name: をはじめ: starting with
points.can_do_en: Can name a leading example with をはじめ.
points.example: 社長をはじめ、全員が出席しました。
points.example_en: Everyone attended, starting with the president.

points.name: にかけては・にわたって
points.can_do_en: Can say range and field with にわたって and にかけては.
points.example: 三日間にわたって、会議が開かれました。
points.example_en: The meeting was held over three days.

points.name: ばかりか・だけでなく
points.can_do_en: Can add an extra point with ばかりか.
points.example: 彼は英語ばかりか、中国語も話せます。
points.example_en: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

points.name: うえに: besides
points.can_do_en: Can add another point with うえに.
points.example: この店は安いうえに、おいしいです。
points.example_en: This shop is cheap, and delicious too.

points.name: うえで: upon, in doing
points.can_do_en: Can say when or in doing something with うえで.
points.example: 契約するうえで、注意が必要です。
points.example_en: Care is needed when signing a contract.

points.name: 反面・一方で: on the other hand
points.can_do_en: Can show two sides with 反面 and 一方で.
points.example: 便利な反面、危険もあります。
points.example_en: It is convenient, but also has risks.

points.name: かわりに: instead
points.can_do_en: Can say instead of, or in exchange for, with かわりに.
points.example: 肉のかわりに、豆腐を使います。
points.example_en: I use tofu instead of meat.

points.name: にもかかわらず: despite
points.can_do_en: Can say despite with にもかかわらず.
points.example: 雨にもかかわらず、大勢の人が集まりました。
points.example_en: Despite the rain, many people gathered.

points.name: くせに: despite (criticism)
points.can_do_en: Can criticise someone for an inconsistency with くせに.
points.example: 知っているくせに、教えてくれません。
points.example_en: He knows, yet won't tell me.

points.name: ものの・とはいえ
points.can_do_en: Can concede a point with ものの.
points.example: 頭では分かっているものの、行動できません。
points.example_en: I understand it in my head, but I can't act on it.

points.name: ながらも: while still
points.can_do_en: Can say although with ながらも.
points.example: 貧しいながらも、幸せに暮らしました。
points.example_en: They lived happily, though poor.

points.name: ところが・それなのに
points.can_do_en: Can express surprising outcomes with ところが.
points.example: 早く着いた。ところが、店は閉まっていた。
points.example_en: I arrived early. But the shop was closed.

points.name: だけあって・だけに
points.can_do_en: Can say a result fits its cause with だけあって.
points.example: 専門家だけあって、詳しいですね。
points.example_en: As expected of an expert, you know the details.

points.name: おかげで・せいで・ために
points.can_do_en: Can say positive and negative causes with おかげで and せいで.
points.example: 薬のおかげで、すぐ治りました。
points.example_en: Thanks to the medicine, I recovered quickly.

points.name: からこそ・ばこそ
points.can_do_en: Can stress a reason with からこそ.
points.example: 努力したからこそ、成功しました。
points.example_en: It is precisely because I made an effort that I succeeded.

points.name: ばかりに・ために
points.can_do_en: Can say a regretful cause with ばかりに.
points.example: 油断したばかりに、失敗しました。
points.example_en: Just because I let my guard down, I failed.

points.name: とたん・や否や
points.can_do_en: Can say that one thing happens right after another.
points.example: ドアを開けたとたん、猫が飛び出しました。
points.example_en: The moment I opened the door, the cat darted out.

points.name: ないうちに・ているうちに
points.can_do_en: Can say before it changes or while it is happening.
points.example: 暗くならないうちに帰りましょう。
points.example_en: Let's go home before it gets dark.

points.name: つつ・つつある
points.can_do_en: Can say simultaneity or ongoing change in written style.
points.example: 景気は回復しつつあります。
points.example_en: The economy is gradually recovering.

points.name: ば〜ほど: the more, the more
points.can_do_en: Can say proportional change with ば〜ほど.
points.example: 読めば読むほど、面白くなります。
points.example_en: The more I read, the more interesting it gets.

points.name: どころか・どころではない
points.can_do_en: Can deny and go further with どころか.
points.example: 忙しくて、休むどころではありません。
points.example_en: I'm so busy that resting is out of the question.

points.name: たまま・っぱなし: left as is
points.can_do_en: Can say that a state continues unchanged.
points.example: 電気をつけたまま、寝てしまいました。
points.example_en: I fell asleep with the light on.

points.name: ところだった: nearly
points.can_do_en: Can say that something almost happened with ところだった.
points.example: もう少しで遅刻するところでした。
points.example_en: I almost arrived late.

points.name: かける・きる・つづける・だす
points.can_do_en: Can build compound aspects with かける, きる and だす.
points.example: この本は三日で読みきれます。
points.example_en: I can read this book through in three days.

points.name: ように言う・頼む・注意する
points.can_do_en: Can report orders and requests with ように.
points.example: 先生は静かにするように言いました。
points.example_en: The teacher told us to be quiet.

points.name: ようになっている・ことになっている
points.can_do_en: Can describe rules and customs with ことになっている.
points.example: ここでは靴を脱ぐことになっています。
points.example_en: Here, one is supposed to take off one's shoes.

points.name: にちがいない: surely
points.can_do_en: Can state a strong conviction with にちがいない.
points.example: 彼は犯人にちがいありません。
points.example_en: He must be the culprit.

points.name: おそれがある・かねない
points.can_do_en: Can warn about risks with おそれがある and かねない.
points.example: 台風で被害が出るおそれがあります。
points.example_en: There is a risk of damage from the typhoon.

points.name: かねる・がたい: hard to
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is hard to do with かねる and がたい.
points.example: その意見には賛成しかねます。
points.example_en: I cannot agree with that opinion.

points.name: ざるを得ない: have no choice
points.can_do_en: Can say that there is no alternative.
points.example: 会社の命令なので、行かざるを得ません。
points.example_en: It is a company order, so I have no choice but to go.

points.name: ないわけにはいかない
points.can_do_en: Can say that you cannot avoid doing something.
points.example: 今日は出席しないわけにはいきません。
points.example_en: I can't avoid attending today.

points.name: ないではいられない・ずにはいられない
points.can_do_en: Can say that you cannot help doing something.
points.example: その話を聞いて、笑わずにはいられませんでした。
points.example_en: Hearing that story, I couldn't help laughing.

points.name: てたまらない・てしかたがない
points.can_do_en: Can say that a feeling is unbearable with てたまらない.
points.example: 眠くてたまりません。
points.example_en: I'm unbearably sleepy.

points.name: たがる・がる: third-person desire
points.can_do_en: Can describe another person's wish or feeling with たがる and がる.
points.example: 子どもは新しいおもちゃを欲しがります。
points.example_en: The child wants a new toy.

points.name: べからず・てはならない
points.can_do_en: Can recognise written prohibitions.
points.example: 芝生に入るべからず。
points.example_en: Do not enter the lawn.

points.name: てもらえませんか・ていただけませんか
points.can_do_en: Can make polite requests with もらえませんか and いただけませんか.
points.example: 資料を送っていただけませんか。
points.example_en: Could you send me the materials?

points.name: もし〜たら・ば・なら
points.can_do_en: Can state hypotheses with もし.
points.example: もし宝くじに当たったら、世界旅行をします。
points.example_en: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.

points.name: とすれば・としたら・とすると
points.can_do_en: Can say if it is assumed that with としたら.
points.example: 行くとしたら、いつがいいですか。
points.example_en: If we were to go, when would be good?

points.name: たとえ〜ても・としても
points.can_do_en: Can say even supposing that with たとえ〜ても.
points.example: たとえ失敗しても、後悔しません。
points.example_en: Even if I fail, I won't regret it.

points.name: ないかぎり・かぎり
points.can_do_en: Can say unless and as long as with かぎり.
points.example: 雨が降らないかぎり、試合は行われます。
points.example_en: Unless it rains, the match will be held.

points.name: なら〜のに: contrary-to-fact
points.can_do_en: Can regret what is not true with なら〜のに.
points.example: お金があれば、買えるのに。
points.example_en: If I had money, I could buy it.

points.name: さえ〜ば: if only
points.can_do_en: Can say that one condition is enough with さえ〜ば.
points.example: 時間さえあれば、行きたいです。
points.example_en: If only I had time, I would like to go.

points.name: ではないか・じゃないか
points.can_do_en: Can express feeling, confirmation or invitation with じゃないか.
points.example: これは便利じゃないか。
points.example_en: Isn't this convenient!

points.name: ということだ・とのことだ
points.can_do_en: Can report hearsay in formal speech.
points.example: 会議は中止になるということです。
points.example_en: I hear that the meeting will be cancelled.

points.name: ものだ・ものではない
points.can_do_en: Can state general truths or past nostalgia with ものだ.
points.example: 子どものころは、よく川で遊んだものだ。
points.example_en: As a child, I used to play at the river often.

points.name: んじゃない・のではないか
points.can_do_en: Can voice a gentle opinion with のではないか.
points.example: それは間違いではないでしょうか。
points.example_en: Isn't that a mistake?

points.name: かな・かしら・だろうか
points.can_do_en: Can wonder aloud with かな and かしら.
points.example: 明日は晴れるかな。
points.example_en: I wonder if it will be sunny tomorrow.

points.name: on'yomi and kun'yomi
points.can_do_en: Can tell on'yomi and kun'yomi readings of kanji.
points.example: 山の上に、山頂があります。
points.example_en: There is a summit at the top of the mountain.

points.name: compound kanji structure
points.can_do_en: Can understand how two-kanji compounds are built.
points.example: 経済が発展しています。
points.example_en: The economy is developing.

points.name: 〜さ・〜み: nominalizing adjectives
points.can_do_en: Can turn adjectives into nouns with さ and み.
points.example: この橋の長さは百メートルです。
points.example_en: The length of this bridge is one hundred meters.

points.name: prefixes 不・無・非・未
points.can_do_en: Can use the negative prefixes 不, 無, 非 and 未.
points.example: 不便な所に住んでいます。
points.example_en: I live in an inconvenient place.

points.name: loan words and word play
points.can_do_en: Can read loan words and abbreviations.
points.example: スマホでアプリを使います。
points.example_en: I use apps on my smartphone.

points.name: kanji numerals and big numbers
points.can_do_en: Can read numbers written in kanji.
points.example: 売り上げは三千二百万円でした。
points.example_en: Sales were thirty-two million yen.

points.name: passive in news style
points.can_do_en: Can understand passives in news writing.
points.example: 新しい法律が発表されました。
points.example_en: A new law has been announced.

points.name: nominal style in writing
points.can_do_en: Can read formal nominal style used in writing.
points.example: 会議の開催は来週の予定です。
points.example_en: The meeting is scheduled for next week.

points.name: だ・である style in writing
points.can_do_en: Can read and write in the plain written style.
points.example: これは重要な問題である。
points.example_en: This is an important problem.

points.name: softeners and hedges
points.can_do_en: Can soften a statement with hedges such as ちょっと and なかなか.
points.example: それはちょっと難しいですね。
points.example_en: That is a bit difficult.

points.name: giving opinions
points.can_do_en: Can state and soften an opinion in discussion.
points.example: 私の考えでは、この計画は無理だと思います。
points.example_en: In my view, I think this plan is not realistic.

points.name: によって決まる・次第だ
points.can_do_en: Can say that something depends on something with 次第.
points.example: 成功するかどうかは、努力次第です。
points.example_en: Success depends on effort.

points.name: に応じて・に従って
points.can_do_en: Can say in accordance with with に応じて.
points.example: 収入に応じて、税金が決まります。
points.example_en: Taxes are decided according to income.

points.name: にほかならない: nothing but
points.can_do_en: Can state that something is exactly so with にほかならない.
points.example: この成功は努力の結果にほかなりません。
points.example_en: This success is nothing other than the result of effort.

points.name: を余儀なくされる: forced to
points.can_do_en: Can say that circumstances forced an action.
points.example: 会社は事業の縮小を余儀なくされました。
points.example_en: The company was forced to scale down its business.

points.name: にたえる・にたえない
points.can_do_en: Can say worth doing or unbearable to do.
points.example: この映画は鑑賞にたえる作品です。
points.example_en: This film is worth watching.

points.name: にかかわらず・を問わず
points.can_do_en: Can say regardless of with にかかわらず.
points.example: 年齢にかかわらず、誰でも参加できます。
points.example_en: Anyone can take part regardless of age.

points.name: を踏まえて: based on
points.can_do_en: Can say based on with を踏まえて.
points.example: 前回の議論を踏まえて、検討します。
points.example_en: We will consider it based on the previous discussion.

points.name: に際して・にあたって
points.can_do_en: Can say on the occasion of with に際して.
points.example: 入学に際して、書類を提出してください。
points.example_en: On entering the school, please submit the documents.

points.name: をもって: by means of, as of
points.can_do_en: Can mark means or a cut-off point in formal speech.
points.example: 本日をもって、営業を終了いたします。
points.example_en: We will end business as of today.

points.name: に限る・に限って
points.can_do_en: Can say that something is the best or only case.
points.example: 夏はビールに限る。
points.example_en: Nothing beats beer in summer.

points.name: に反して・にそむいて
points.can_do_en: Can say contrary to with に反して.
points.example: 予想に反して、結果は悪かったです。
points.example_en: Contrary to expectation, the result was bad.

points.name: をめぐって・をめぐる
points.can_do_en: Can say concerning a debate with をめぐって.
points.example: この問題をめぐって、意見が分かれています。
points.example_en: Opinions are divided over this issue.

points.name: に至る・に至っては
points.can_do_en: Can say that a situation reaches a point with に至る.
points.example: ついに裁判に至りました。
points.example_en: It finally ended up in court.

points.name: とはいうものの・とはいえ
points.can_do_en: Can concede and qualify with とはいえ.
points.example: 安いとはいえ、品質は悪くありません。
points.example_en: Though cheap, the quality is not bad.

points.name: ところを・ところに
points.can_do_en: Can speak of an interrupted situation with ところを.
points.example: お忙しいところを、ありがとうございます。
points.example_en: Thank you for taking time out of your busy schedule.

points.name: が早いか・なり: as soon as
points.can_do_en: Can say right after with が早いか.
points.example: 電車が止まるが早いか、人々が降りました。
points.example_en: As soon as the train stopped, people got off.

points.name: ばこそ・からには
points.can_do_en: Can say precisely because with ばこそ.
points.example: 家族がいればこそ、頑張れます。
points.example_en: It is only because I have a family that I can do my best.

points.name: からには・以上は: since
points.can_do_en: Can say since it is so with からには.
points.example: 引き受けたからには、最後までやります。
points.example_en: Since I accepted it, I will do it to the end.

points.name: ごとに・たびに
points.can_do_en: Can say every time with ごとに and たびに.
points.example: 会うたびに、彼は元気になっています。
points.example_en: Every time we meet, he is more energetic.

points.name: にあたる・に当たって
points.can_do_en: Can say that something corresponds to something else.
points.example: 今日は祖父の命日にあたります。
points.example_en: Today is the anniversary of my grandfather's death.

points.name: たが最後: once, it is the end
points.can_do_en: Can say that once something happens it is over with たが最後.
points.example: 秘密を話したが最後、噂は広まります。
points.example_en: Once you tell a secret, the rumor spreads.

points.name: たら最後・ようものなら
points.can_do_en: Can warn of a bad outcome with ようものなら.
points.example: 遅れようものなら、叱られます。
points.example_en: If I were to be late, I would get scolded.

points.name: といえども・とはいえ
points.can_do_en: Can concede that even someone or something has limits.
points.example: 専門家といえども、間違えることがあります。
points.example_en: Even experts can make mistakes.

points.name: ようものなら・ないものか
points.can_do_en: Can express a wish that something could be done with ないものか.
points.example: もっと早く着く方法はないものか。
points.example_en: Isn't there some way to get there faster?

points.name: ずにすむ・ないですむ
points.can_do_en: Can say that you can avoid doing something.
points.example: 傘を持っていったので、ぬれずにすみました。
points.example_en: I took an umbrella, so I did not get wet.

points.name: かねない・かねる
points.can_do_en: Can warn of an unwelcome possibility with かねない.
points.example: このままでは、事故を起こしかねません。
points.example_en: At this rate, an accident could happen.

points.name: ようがない・ようがある
points.can_do_en: Can say that there is no way to do something.
points.example: 連絡先が分からないので、連絡しようがありません。
points.example_en: I don't know the contact details, so there is no way to reach out.

points.name: べからず・まじき
points.can_do_en: Can read formal writing that states what must not be done.
points.example: 教師にあるまじき行為です。
points.example_en: It is conduct unbecoming of a teacher.

points.name: passive of feeling and thought
points.can_do_en: Can say how things are thought, called or seen with passives.
points.example: この絵は傑作と言われています。
points.example_en: This painting is said to be a masterpiece.

points.name: させられる: reflections
points.can_do_en: Can describe being moved or made to think with させられる.
points.example: その話を聞いて、深く考えさせられました。
points.example_en: Hearing that story made me think deeply.

points.name: double honorific and over-politeness
points.can_do_en: Can recognise and avoid double honorifics.
points.example: 部長はすでにお帰りになりました。
points.example_en: The department head has already gone home.

points.name: phone and visit keigo
points.can_do_en: Can handle phone calls and visits with proper keigo.
points.example: ただいま席を外しております。
points.example_en: He is away from his desk at the moment.

points.name: honorific and humble adjectives
points.can_do_en: Can use お and ご with adjectives and nouns of respect.
points.example: お忙しい中、ご出席いただき、ありがとうございます。
points.example_en: Thank you for attending in your busy schedule.

points.name: written style なり・ごとし
points.can_do_en: Can read classical-flavored written expressions.
points.example: まるで夢のごとき出来事でした。
points.example_en: It was an event like a dream.

points.name: こと・ものの区別
points.can_do_en: Can tell こと and もの as nominalizers.
points.example: 大切なことは、あきらめないことです。
points.example_en: What matters is not giving up.

points.name: rhetoric: hedging, concession, emphasis
points.can_do_en: Can use hedging and emphasis in discussion.
points.example: 断言はできませんが、可能性は高いと考えられます。
points.example_en: I cannot say for certain, but the possibility seems high.

points.name: dialect: Kansai-ben basics
points.can_do_en: Can recognise common Kansai dialect forms such as ほんま and あかん.
points.example: それはあかんで。
points.example_en: That's no good.

points.name: four-kanji idioms
points.can_do_en: Can understand common four-character idioms.
points.example: 彼は一石二鳥の方法を見つけました。
points.example_en: He found a way to kill two birds with one stone.

points.name: proverbs
points.can_do_en: Can recognise common proverbs.
points.example: 急がば回れと言います。
points.example_en: They say, more haste, less speed.

points.name: idiomatic expressions
points.can_do_en: Can use body-part idioms such as 耳が痛い.
points.example: その話は耳が痛いです。
points.example_en: That story hits home.

points.name: literary and news style reading
points.can_do_en: Can read newspaper and essay style Japanese.
points.example: 政府は新たな対策を発表した。
points.example_en: The government announced new measures.
